boundedQuestion: How can an accepted component remain identity-locked while unfinished sibling components continue to advance in later whole-repository snapshots?

realFailure.observation: A current production correction reported that an older version was opened and edited instead of the designated current version; separately, the user questioned whether whole-version anchoring can accurately preserve already-satisfactory parts.
realFailure.existingCoverage: R2 Golden Baseline plus TASK_FRESHNESS_AND_NO_STALE_DELIVERY_GATE already prohibit stale or wrong-parent delivery.
realFailure.gap: The current whole-commit anchor cannot express that component A is accepted and protected while component B remains intentionally open for iteration.
realFailure.regressionDecision: Do not create a duplicate stale-delivery regression. Reuse TERRAIN_NO_STALE_DELIVERY_001 for wrong-target lineage and add this component-scope replay as candidate evidence only.

teacher.name: Git object data model
teacher.exactQuestionAnswered: Git represents a commit as a snapshot rooted in a tree; tree entries identify child blobs or subtrees, so a component can be identity-checked independently of the whole snapshot.
teacher.whatItKnowsBeyondCurrentBestView: KAOPU already pins an accepted whole-repository commit. Git's blob/tree/commit separation supplies the missing transferable mechanism for a normalized, path-scoped accepted-component manifest that can remain constant while an unrelated subtree advances.

sources.fact: Tree entries associate filenames with blob or subtree object IDs; commit objects point to a top-level tree snapshot.
Git objects are immutable and have object IDs; blobs, trees, and commits have distinct roles.
Git documents SHA-1 and SHA-256 object naming and SHA-256 repository format transition.

candidateMethod.name: Component-Scoped Golden Baseline Manifest
candidateMethod.role: Complement the whole-commit Golden Baseline; never replace it.

gateSemantics.COMPONENT_BASELINE_CONFIRMED: Protected component digest matches; unrelated allowed sibling paths may advance.
gateSemantics.HOLD_PROTECTED_COMPONENT_CHANGED: Protected component digest changed without explicit reopen authorization.
gateSemantics.HOLD_COMPONENT_IDENTITY_UNKNOWN: Required path, digest, or acceptance evidence is missing or ambiguous.
gateSemantics.REOPENED_BY_USER_OR_COORDINATOR: The accepted component was explicitly reopened with a new Task Anchor and reason.

routingFields.verifierGate: Producer may not self-authorize a protected-component digest change.

minimalReplay.finding: Both candidates advance the whole snapshot. The component manifest passes the candidate that changes only the unfinished sibling and holds the candidate that also changes the accepted component.

boundaries: A digest proves identity, not visual or semantic quality.
Use an explicit SHA-256 payload digest in the manifest; do not treat a legacy Git SHA-1 object ID as a standalone security guarantee.
Git LFS pointer identity is not the same as the referenced payload identity; hash the payload separately.
Submodule commit pins, generated outputs, runtime/browser state, device captures, and nondeterministic builds require separate artifact receipts.
Normalize paths, symlinks, renames, case sensitivity, and file modes before computing a component scope.
A component may be reopened only through explicit user/coordinator authorization; no silent scope widening.

decision.scope: Candidate-only; one-Mother historical replay before any OS or global gate change.
decision.rollbackPoint: Keep R2 whole-commit Golden Baseline as sole Current Best View if the component manifest does not reduce protected-part regressions without blocking legitimate sibling iteration.
